- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–7 days, especially if sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and model still forecasts high prices, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 7–14 days; avoid overconfidence in bullish sentiment.  
- Model often overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is mixed or neutral — apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum followed by a sharp drop, model tends to lag — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33 to 0.67), model often overfits short-term noise — apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 7–14 days.
